# secopsctl cases

Manage SOAR cases: read (list, get) and guarded triage (assign, tag, close, ...)

## cases aging

Read-only: open cases by age (oldest first) with SLA status

```text
secopsctl cases aging [--filter <expr>] [--limit N] [flags]
```

```text
List open cases oldest-first by age (now − createTime), with priority and SLA
expiration status — the queue-health view for spotting stale/aging cases.
--filter composes with the open-status base. JSON or table.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--filter` | string | - | extra server-side filter (composed with status = 'OPENED') |
| `--limit` | int | 25 | max rows to show (0 = all) |
| `--max` | int | 2000 | max cases to scan |

## cases alert close

Close one alert in a case (the case stays open)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl cases alert close --id N --alert <ident> --reason <enum> [flags]
```

```text
Close a single alert without closing its case — the surgical false-positive
path. --reason: malicious | not-malicious | maintenance | inconclusive
(alerts take no 'unknown'). --usefulness feeds the alert-usefulness stats.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alert` | string | - | alert identifier, as printed by 'soar case get' (required) |
| `--comment` | string | - | close comment (free-text note) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--id` | int | 0 | SOAR case id (required) |
| `--reason` | string | - | close reason: malicious \| not-malicious \| maintenance \| inconclusive (required) |
| `--root-cause` | string | - | close root cause — list options with 'soar case values root-causes' |
| `--usefulness` | string | - | alert usefulness stat: none \| useful \| not-useful |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## cases alert move

Move one alert out of a case (to another case, or a new one)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl cases alert move --id N --alert <ident> [--to M] [flags]
```

```text
Split a mis-grouped alert out of its case — the inverse of `soar case merge`.
With --to the alert moves into that existing case; without it the platform
creates a new case for the alert.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alert` | string | - | alert identifier, as printed by 'soar case get' (required) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--id` | int | 0 | SOAR case id (required) |
| `--to` | int | 0 | destination case id (omit to move the alert into a new case) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## cases alert priority

Change one alert's priority

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl cases alert priority --id N --alert <ident> --priority <level> [flags]
```

```text
Re-prioritize a single alert within its case. At apply time the alert's
name and current priority are resolved from the case (the request wants
both), so a wrong --alert fails on that read before any mutation.
```

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alert` | string | - | alert identifier, as printed by 'soar case get' (required) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--id` | int | 0 | SOAR case id (required) |
| `--priority` | string | - | target priority: informative\|low\|medium\|high\|critical (required) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## cases close

Close a single case (typed reason enum, same vocabulary as `soar push bulk-close`)

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl cases close --id N --reason <enum> [flags]
```

```text
Close one case. --reason is the fixed close-reason enum (the same set
`soar push bulk-close` uses) so single and bulk closes aggregate in metrics:
malicious | not-malicious | maintenance | inconclusive | unknown. Put your
custom root-cause name in --root-cause and any free-text note in --comment.
--id is the SOAR integer case id from `soar case list`. Guarded: dry-run by
default, --yes to apply live.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alert` | string | - | scope the action to one alert in the case instead of the whole case (alert identifier from 'soar case get <id>'); omit to act on the case |
| `--comment` | string | - | close comment (free-text note) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--id` | int | 0 | SOAR case id (required) |
| `--reason` | string | - | close reason: malicious \| not-malicious \| maintenance \| inconclusive \| unknown (required) |
| `--root-cause` | string | - | close root cause (your custom root-cause name) — list options with 'soar case values root-causes' |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

**Examples**

```bash
# preview closing a false positive (dry run)
  secopsctl soar case close --id 1234 --reason not-malicious

  # apply for real with a note
  secopsctl soar case close --id 1234 --reason malicious \
      --comment 'confirmed C2 beacon' --yes
```

## cases counts

Read-only: case counts grouped by priority for a filter set

```text
secopsctl cases counts [--filter <expr>] [flags]
```

```text
The triage queue's per-priority numbers: one cheap exact count per priority
(the modern cases list reports the full filtered total on a pageSize=1
request; the cases:countPriorities RPC is not served). --filter composes
with the per-priority term, e.g. "status = 'OPENED'" (the default) or
"status = 'OPENED' and (assignee = '@Tier1')".
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--filter` | string | status = 'OPENED' | base server-side filter the per-priority counts compose with |

## cases list

Read-only: list SOAR cases (default: open) with triage filters

```text
secopsctl cases list [flags]
```

```text
List SOAR cases (first page) as a compact table, or raw JSON. Reads only —
no LIVE banner. Use the case id shown here with `soar case get` and the
mutating verbs.

Triage filters: --assignee (substring), --priority, --tag, --since narrow the
fetched page client-side on both lanes (--tag needs the modern lane; --since
matches the case's update time, or creation time on the legacy queue).
--filter passes a verbatim server-side filter expression to the modern
v1alpha cases API (e.g. "status = 'OPENED'").

Uses the modern v1alpha cases API by default, falling back to the legacy
AppKey queue on error. --legacy forces the legacy queue only.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--assignee` | string | - | keep cases whose assignee contains this (case-insensitive) |
| `--filter` | string | - | verbatim server-side filter for the modern cases API |
| `--limit` | int | 100 | max cases to fetch/show (first page; 0 = up to 100) |
| `--priority` | string | - | keep cases at this priority: informative\|low\|medium\|high\|critical |
| `--since` | string | - | keep cases updated since (duration like 24h, RFC3339, or YYYY-MM-DD) |
| `--sort` | string | - | client-side sort (modern lane): priority (worst first) \| created \| updated (newest first) |
| `--status` | string | open | status filter: open\|closed\|all |
| `--tag` | string | - | keep cases carrying this tag (modern lane only) |

**Examples**

```bash
# open cases (the default)
  secopsctl soar case list

  # high-priority cases assigned to an analyst
  secopsctl soar case list --priority high --assignee analyst

  # server-side filter, machine-readable
  secopsctl soar case list --filter "status = 'OPENED'" --json
```

```bash
  secopsctl soar case playbook-errors 6139 --alert <alert-identifier>
```

## cases run-action

MUTATING (guarded): execute an integration action on a case

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl cases run-action --id N --action <name> --instance <uuid> [flags]
```

```text
Run a single integration action (e.g. HTTP_Post Data, Ping, Enrich IP)
against a case. This is the ad-hoc counterpart to a playbook step — any
installed action can be triggered directly.

  secopsctl soar case run-action --id 123 --action HTTP_Ping \
    --instance <uuid> --alert <alert-group-id>

Script parameters are passed via --param key=value (repeatable); secrets
use env-var references (--param 'URL=env:WEBHOOK_URL'). The alert group
identifier comes from `soar case get <id> --json`
(alerts[].additionalProperties.alertGroupIdentifier).

For a MARKETPLACE integration's action (e.g. GoogleChronicle's Ping / Get Data
Tables), pass --integration <id> so the action is sent as <id>_<action>
(GoogleChronicle_Ping) — the qualified name the API resolves a script by; a bare
name fails. Built-in Scripts actions are already qualified (HTTP_Ping), so omit
--integration for those.

Returns the action result (resultCode, message, resultJsonObject).
Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply.

The run is always scoped to an alert group — the server rejects a run that
carries none (a missing scope returns HTTP 500, an empty one 400). Pass --alert
with an alertGroupIdentifier from `soar case get --json`, or omit it and the
action is scoped to the case's alert automatically.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--action` | string | - | integration action name, e.g. HTTP_Ping or HTTP_Post Data (required) |
| `--alert` | string | - | alertGroupIdentifier to scope the action (from 'soar case get --json'); required by the server, so when omitted it is auto-resolved from the case's alert(s) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--id` | int | 0 | SOAR case id (required) — from 'soar case list' |
| `--instance` | string | - | integration instance UUID (required; from 'integrations instances') |
| `--integration` | string | - | integration identifier for a marketplace action (e.g. GoogleChronicle) — the action is sent as <integration>_<action> (GoogleChronicle_Ping); omit for built-in Scripts actions whose name is already qualified (HTTP_Ping) |
| `--param` | stringArray | - | key=value script parameter (repeatable); use env:VAR for secrets |
| `--scope` | string | All entities | entity scope |
| `--skip-validate` | bool | false | skip the pre-flight check of --param against the action's schema (--integration actions only) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alert-field` | stringArray | - | additional alert fields as key=value (repeatable) |
| `--alert-name` | string | - | alert name for the simulation (required) |
| `--alert-product` | string | - | alert product (required) |
| `--alert-source` | string | - | alert source (required) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--event-field` | stringArray | - | additional event fields as key=value (repeatable) |
| `--event-name` | string | - | event name (required) |
| `--rule-name` | string | - | rule name that triggers the alert (required) |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## cases soar-id

Read-only: resolve SIEM case uuid(s) to SOAR integer case id(s)

```text
secopsctl cases soar-id <case-uuid> [<case-uuid>...]
```

```text
Resolve one or more SIEM case uuids (e.g. an alert's caseName from
`alerts list --json`) to their SOAR integer case ids via legacyBatchGetCases —
the id `soar case get` and the mutating case verbs take. One case, two ids:
this is the bridge between them.
```

## cases stage

Change a case's (or many cases') stage

> Guarded mutation — dry-run by default; apply with `--yes`.

```text
secopsctl cases stage (--id N | --ids 1,2,3) --stage <s> [flags]
```

```text
Move one or more cases to a workflow stage (list valid stages with
`soar case values stages`). --id is the SOAR integer case id from
`soar case list`; --ids moves a whole set in one bulk call
(ExecuteBulkChangeCaseStage). Guarded: dry-run by default, --yes to apply.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--alert` | string | - | scope a single-case stage change to one alert (ignored with --ids) |
| `--dry-run` | bool | false | preview only (default behavior) |
| `--id` | int | 0 | SOAR case id |
| `--ids` | string | - | comma-separated case ids (bulk form) |
| `--stage` | string | - | target stage (required) — list valid stages with 'soar case values stages' |
| `--yes` | bool | false | apply for real / skip confirmation |

## cases stats

Read-only: queue stats — open/closed counts, age + resolution-time percentiles

```text
secopsctl cases stats [--filter <expr>] [flags]
```

```text
Compute queue health over the scanned cases: open vs closed counts, open-case
age p50/p90 (now − createTime), and closed-case resolution-time p50/p90
(updateTime − createTime, a close-time proxy — the case payload has no
separate detection/close timestamp, so this is resolution, not MTTD). --filter
narrows the scanned set. JSON or table.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--filter` | string | - | server-side filter to scope the scanned cases |
| `--max` | int | 2000 | max cases to scan |

```text
List the configured values an operator can pass to the case verbs:
```

## cases workload

Read-only: open-case load per analyst (queue distribution)

```text
secopsctl cases workload [--filter <expr>] [flags]
```

```text
Group open cases by assignee and count them — who is carrying how much of
the queue, for load-balancing and shift planning. --filter composes with the
open-status base (e.g. "priority = 'PRIORITY_HIGH'"). JSON or table.
```

**Flags**

| Flag | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--filter` | string | - | extra server-side filter (composed with status = 'OPENED') |
| `--max` | int | 2000 | max cases to scan |
